newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Tveruniversalbank to resume some operations.
newsitem.headline: Russia Tveruniversalbank to resume some operations.

text.p: Russia's central bank has given troubled Tveruniversalbank permission to carry out some banking operations in order to sell assets and pay off its debts, a senior central bank official said on Wednesday.
"We hope the bank will pay its creditors and restore its solvency," central bank deputy chairman Alexander Turbanov told a news conference.

The central bank revoked Tveruniversalbank's licence in July and imposed a year-long temporary management on it in October after central bankers found liquidity problems at the bank, formerly Russia's 17th largest.
Turbanov said bank branches in Tver, located between Moscow and St Petersburg, and Moscow would be allowed to carry out limited transactions with the central bank and clients.
Tveruniversalbank is still prohibited from working with new clients, granting new credits, carrying out operations with precious metals, carry out trust operations and buying new shares, he said.
It is also prohibited from opening new branches and representation offices and from opening and serving accounts of commercial banks, he said.

Sergei Panov, head of the central bank re-organisation department, said temporary management would begin implementing a re-organisation plan, if Tveruniversalbank's creditors approved the plan at a meeting scheduled for January 15.
The plan provides for accumulation of funds to pay creditors and reduction of creditors' demands for repayment, currently 1.7 trillion roubles.
Nikolai Zakharov, a central bank official who heads the temporary administration, said the administration had fully re-organised Tveruniversalbank's Moscow branch.

"If the assets are sold normally, they will fully cover the liabilities," he said. "The bank has enough of assets, including highly-liquid assets. Non-Moscow branches of the bank have a liquid credits portfolio, including real estate."
